literal: Grand Commandant Man Chong died.
idiomatic: Grand Commandant Man Chong passed away.

literal: In the sixth year, eighth month, day Wuwu, a comet appeared at the Seven Stars, two feet long, white in color, advanced to Zhang, and was extinguished after twenty-three days.
idiomatic: Year six, August, wuwu: a white two-foot comet moved from the Seven Stars to Zhang and vanished in twenty-three days.

literal: In the seventh year, eleventh month, day Guihai, it again appeared in the Chariot, one foot long, and was extinguished after one hundred fifty-six days.
idiomatic: Year seven, November, guihai: another comet in the Chariot lasted one hundred fifty-six days.

literal: In the ninth year’s third month, it again appeared in the Hairy Head, six feet long, bluish white, its ray pointing southwest.
idiomatic: Year nine, March: a six-foot bluish-white comet in the Pleiades aimed its tail southwest.

literal: In the seventh month, it again appeared in the Wings, two feet long, advanced to the Chariot, and was extinguished after forty-two days.
idiomatic: July: a two-foot comet in the Wings crept to the Chariot and died out in forty-two days.

literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "The Seven Stars and Zhang are Zhou’s field allotment; Wings and Chariot are Chu; the Hairy Head is Zhao and Wei."
idiomatic: Commentary maps the Seven Stars and Zhang to Zhou, Wings and Chariot to Chu, and the Pleiades to Zhao-Wei.

literal: Comets thereby remove the old and spread the new; they govern arms and mourning.
idiomatic: Comets scour away the old order and foretell war and death.

literal: In the first Jiaping year, the August Lord executed Cao Shuang and his younger brothers and their partisans, all exterminating three clans; the capital was under strict arms.
idiomatic: Jiaping one: Sima Yi slew Cao Shuang’s faction to the third degree and locked down Luoyang.

literal: In the third year, he executed the Prince of Chu, Biao, and also struck Wang Ling in Huainan.
idiomatic: Year three: Prince Biao of Chu died and Wang Ling was crushed in Huainan.

literal: Huainan is eastern Chu.
idiomatic: Huainan counts as eastern Chu territory.

literal: Wei’s princes were confined at Ye.
idiomatic: Wei imperial princes were imprisoned at Ye.

literal: In Jiaping third year, eleventh month, day Guihai, there was a broom star in Encampment, moving west, extinguished after ninety days.
idiomatic: Jiaping three, November, guihai: a ninety-day western broom star in Encampment.

literal: The prognostication states: "There will be arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and funerals follow.

literal: Encampment is the rear palace; the rear palace will moreover have disorder.
idiomatic: Encampment marks the harem, which now faces turmoil.

literal: In the fourth year, second month, day Dingyou, a comet appeared in the west, in the Stomach, five or six rods long, white in color, its ray pointing south, piercing Orion, extinguished after twenty days.
idiomatic: Year four, February, dingyou: a huge white western comet in the Stomach pierced Orion and faded in twenty days.

literal: In the fifth year’s eleventh month, a comet again appeared in the Chariot, five rods long, west of the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s Left Law Enforcer, pointing southeast, extinguished after one hundred ninety days.
idiomatic: Year five, November: a five-rod comet in the Chariot west of the Left Law Enforcer lingered one hundred ninety days.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "The Stomach is Yan Province’s field allotment."
idiomatic: Commentary ties the Stomach to Yanzhou.

literal: Orion governs arms.
idiomatic: Orion’s Belt stars govern warfare.

literal: The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court.
idiomatic: The enclosure is the celestial court of the sovereign.

literal: The Law Enforcer is the wielder of government.
idiomatic: Law Enforcer stars mark chief ministers.

literal: Brooms and comets are images of arms and mourning, removing the old and spreading the new.
idiomatic: Comets signal war, death, and dynastic turnover.

literal: In the first Zhengyuan year’s second month, Li Feng, Feng’s younger brother Yi, the empress’s father Zhang Ji, and others plotted rebellion; all were executed; the empress was also deposed.
idiomatic: Zhengyuan one, February: Li Feng, Li Yi, Zhang Ji, and co. fell to execution and the empress was cast down.

literal: In the ninth month, the emperor was deposed and made Prince of Qi.
idiomatic: September: the emperor was demoted to Prince of Qi.

literal: In the first Zhengyuan year of the Duke of Gaoxiang Township, eleventh month, white vapor issued beside the Southern Dipper, several rods wide, its length spanning the sky.
idiomatic: Gaoxiang Duke Zhengyuan one, November: white qi flared beside the Dipper, yards wide and sky-long.

literal: Wang Su states: "It is the banner of Chiyou; will the southeast have turmoil?"
idiomatic: Wang Su calls it Chiyou’s war-banner and asks if the southeast will riot.

literal: In the second year’s first month, there was a comet seen in Wu and Chu’s division, stretching northwest across the sky.
idiomatic: Year two, first month: a comet filled the Wu-Chu sector northwestward.

literal: Eastern-stabilizing Grand General Wuqiu Jian and others held Huainan in rebellion; the Brilliant Emperor campaigned and pacified them.
idiomatic: Wuqiu Jian seized Huainan until Sima Shi crushed the revolt.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "When Chiyou’s banner appears, the king campaigns in the four directions."
idiomatic: The Chiyou-banner gloss means the sovereign sends armies everywhere.

literal: Afterward he again campaigned against Huainan and pacified Ba and Shu in the west.
idiomatic: Later campaigns hit Huainan again and subdued Ba-Shu.

literal: That year was also Wu ruler Sun Liang’s first Wufeng year.
idiomatic: The same year was Sun Liang of Wu’s Wufeng era.

literal: Dipper and Ox are Wu and Yue’s division.
idiomatic: The Dipper-Ox zone marks Wu-Yue.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "Wu will have arms and mourning; it is an image of removing the old and spreading the new."
idiomatic: Commentary says Wu faces war and renewal.

literal: In the third Taiping year, Sun Chen massed troops and surrounded the palace, deposing Liang as Prince of Kuaiji; therefore the "National Records" also records it under Wu.
idiomatic: Taiping three: Sun Chen besieged the palace, demoted Sun Liang to Prince of Kuaiji, so the chronicle logs it for Wu too.

literal: Huainan and Jiangdong share Yangzhou ground; therefore at that time the anomaly appeared in Wu and Chu.
idiomatic: Huainan and Jiangdong both lie in Yangzhou, so the sign showed in Wu-Chu.

literal: Chu’s division in Wei is Huainan, which mostly shares calamities with Wu.
idiomatic: Wei’s Huainan sector mirrors Wu’s omens.

literal: Therefore Wuqiu Jian took the comet as answering to himself, thereupon raised troops and was defeated.
idiomatic: Wuqiu Jian read the comet as his own sign, rose anyway, and lost.

literal: Three years later, that is Wei’s second Ganlu year, Zhuge Dan again rebelled in Huainan; Wu sent generals to rescue him.
idiomatic: Three years on, Ganlu two: Zhuge Dan rebelled in Huainan with Wu relief columns.

literal: When the city fell, Dan’s host and Wu’s troops each died or drowned in the tens of thousands, still matching the earlier long comet.
idiomatic: At the fall tens of thousands of Dan’s and Wu’s soldiers perished—fulfilling the long-comet omen.

literal: In Ganlu second year, eleventh month, a comet appeared in the Horn, white in color.
idiomatic: Ganlu two, November: a white comet in the Horn.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a comet appears between the two Horns and is white, armies rise without battle and the state has great mourning."
idiomatic: A white comet between the Horns means armies mass without fighting and the dynasty mourns deeply.

literal: In the first Jingyuan year, the Duke of Gaoxiang Township was killed by Cheng Ji.
idiomatic: Jingyuan one: Cao Mao fell to Cheng Ji’s blade.

literal: In the fourth year, tenth month, day Dingchou, a guest star appeared inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure, turned moving southeast, passed through the Chariot station, and was extinguished after seven days.
idiomatic: Year four, October, dingchou: a week-long guest star drifted through the enclosure toward the Chariot.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a guest star exits the Supreme Palace Enclosure, there will be arms and mourning."
idiomatic: Guest stars leaving the enclosure mean war and death.

literal: In the first Jingyuan year, the Duke of Gaoxiang Township was murdered.
idiomatic: Jingyuan one repeated Cao Mao’s assassination.

literal: In Yuan Di’s third Jingyuan year, eleventh month, day Renyin, a comet appeared in the Neck, white in color, five inches long, turned moving north, extinguished after forty-five days.
idiomatic: Wei Emperor Yuan, Jingyuan three, November, renyin: a five-inch white comet in the Neck moved north forty-five days.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and funerals again.

literal: One gloss says: "When a comet appears in the Neck, the Son of Heaven loses virtue."
idiomatic: A variant warns the ruler loses moral mandate.

literal: In the fourth year, Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu and conquered it.
idiomatic: Year four: Zhong Hui and Deng Ai took Shu.

literal: The two generals rebelled and were disorderly; both were executed.
idiomatic: Both generals mutinied and died under sentence.

literal: In the second Xianxi year, fifth month, a comet appeared at Wang Liang, more than a rod long, white in color, pointing southeast, extinguished after twelve days.
idiomatic: Xianxi two, May: a white, yard-long comet at Wang Liang pointed southeast twelve days.

literal: The prognostication states: "Wang Liang is the Son of Heaven’s chariot-team."
idiomatic: Wang Liang marks the royal charioteer stars.

literal: A comet sweeping it is a sign of abdication in favor of another, an image of removing the old and spreading the new.
idiomatic: A comet brushing Wang Liang foretells abdication and regime change.

literal: White color means mourning.
idiomatic: White comets add mourning.

literal: Wang Liang is in the eastern Wall lodge; it is also Bing Province’s field allotment.
idiomatic: Wang Liang sits in Wall and ties to Bingzhou’s celestial field.

literal: In the eighth month, Emperor Wen died.
idiomatic: August: King Wen (Sima Zhao) died, clearing the way for usurpation.

literal: In the twelfth month, Emperor Wu received Wei’s abdication.
idiomatic: December: Sima Yan accepted Wei’s abdication.

literal: In Emperor Wu’s fourth Taishi year, first month, day Bingxu, a comet appeared in the Chariot, greenish white, moving northwest, then turning east.
idiomatic: Jin Taishi four, first month, bingxu: a green-white comet in the Chariot drifted northwest then east.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning; the Chariot is also Chu’s field allotment."
idiomatic: War and death, with Chu’s field implicated.

literal: In the third month, Empress Dowager Wang died.
idiomatic: March: Empress Dowager Wang passed away.

literal: In the tenth month, Wu raided Jiangxia and Xiangyang.
idiomatic: October: Wu struck Jiangxia and Xiangyang.

literal: In the fifth year’s ninth month, a star broomed the Purple Palace.
idiomatic: Year five, September: a broom star swept the Purple Palace.

literal: The prognostication was as above.
idiomatic: The usual Purple Palace gloss applied.

literal: The Purple Palace is the Son of Heaven’s inner palace.
idiomatic: The Purple Palace is the celestial inner court.

literal: In the tenth year, Empress Yang the Martial Origin died.
idiomatic: Year ten: Empress Yang Wu yuan died.

literal: In the tenth year’s twelfth month, there was a star brooming in the Chariot.
idiomatic: Year ten, December: a broom star in the Chariot.

literal: The prognostication states: "Under Heaven arms will arise; the Chariot is also Chu’s field allotment."
idiomatic: Realm-wide war looms; the Chariot again marks Chu.

literal: In the second Xianning year, sixth month, day Jiaxu, a star broomed in the Root.
idiomatic: Xianning two, June, jiaxu: a broom star in the Root.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven loses virtue and changes governance."
idiomatic: The throne loses virtue and shifts policy.

literal: The Root is also Yan Province’s division.
idiomatic: The Root also maps to Yanzhou.

literal: In the seventh month, a star broomed the Great Horn.
idiomatic: July: a broom star swept Arcturus.

literal: The Great Horn is the emperor’s seat.
idiomatic: Arcturus is the celestial throne.

literal: In the eighth month, a star broomed the Supreme Palace Enclosure, reaching the Wings, Northern Dipper, and Three Steps.
idiomatic: August: a broom ran through the enclosure to Wings, the Dipper, and Three Steps.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; great men find it ominous."
idiomatic: The enclosure warns great lords of ill omen.

literal: One gloss says: "There will be change of king."
idiomatic: A variant predicts a new king.

literal: The Wings are also Chu’s field allotment.
idiomatic: Wings again mark Chu.

literal: The Northern Dipper governs killing and punishment; the Three Steps are the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: The Dipper rules executions; the Three Steps are the three dukes.

literal: In the third year’s first month, a star broomed in the west.
idiomatic: Year three, first month: a western broom star.

literal: In the third month, a star broomed in the Stomach.
idiomatic: March: a broom in the Stomach.

literal: The Stomach is Xu Province’s division.
idiomatic: The Stomach maps to Xuzhou.

literal: In the fourth month, a star broomed the Woman Attendant.
idiomatic: April: a broom crossed the Woman Attendant stars.

literal: The Woman Attendant is the rear palace.
idiomatic: Those stars mark the harem.

literal: In the fifth month, it again broomed in the east.
idiomatic: May: another eastern broom.

literal: In the seventh month, a star broomed the Purple Palace.
idiomatic: July: a broom swept the Purple Palace.

literal: The superior gloss states: "Under Heaven the ruler will change."
idiomatic: High commentary reads: the throne changes hands.

literal: In the fourth year’s fourth month, Chiyou’s banner appeared in the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: Year four, April: Chiyou’s banner showed in the Eastern Well.

literal: After two years the dynasty tilted three fronts to campaign against Wu; this was its response.
idiomatic: Two years later the tripartite assault on Wu matched the sign.

literal: In the fifth year’s third month, a star broomed in the Willow.
idiomatic: Year five, March: a broom in the Willow.

literal: In the fourth month, it again broomed in the Woman Attendant.
idiomatic: April: another sweep of the Woman Attendant.

literal: In the seventh month, it broomed in the Purple Palace.
idiomatic: July: the Purple Palace was broomed again.

literal: The prognostication states: "Outer ministers encroach on the ruler."
idiomatic: Border ministers bully the throne.

literal: The Willow is also the Three Rivers’ field allotment.
idiomatic: The Willow marks the Three Rivers zone.

literal: The Great Horn, Supreme Palace Enclosure, Purple Palace, and Woman Attendant all stand for the king.
idiomatic: Arcturus, the enclosure, Purple Palace, and Woman Attendant all image the sovereign.

literal: The next year Wu perished; this was its response.
idiomatic: Next year Wu fell—exactly as foretold.

literal: Brooming governs arms and mourning.
idiomatic: Broom stars mean war and death.

literal: In the Wu campaign, the hosts of the Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan all marched out, battling in Wu-Chu lands; Wu’s chancellor and area commanders down were beheaded by the dozen, while subordinate officers and rank-and-file lost heads by the myriad—all were its signs.
idiomatic: The conquest of Wu threw Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan armies into Wu-Chu fighting, beheading Wu’s command stack by the dozen and common soldiers by the myriad—each tally matched the omens.

literal: In the second Taikang year’s eighth month, a star broomed in Zhang.
idiomatic: Taikang two, August: a broom star in Zhang.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and mourning follow.

literal: In the eleventh month, a star broomed at the Coachman’s yoke-stars.
idiomatic: November: a broom crossed the Coachman’s yoke (reading 斬轅 as the Coachman carriage stars).

literal: The prognostication states: "The rear palace will answer for it."
idiomatic: The harem bears the omen.

literal: In the fourth year’s third month, day Wushen, a star broomed in the southwest.
idiomatic: Year four, March, wushen: a broom star in the southwest.
